  "text": "By morning, the harbor had settled. Crates lay splintered along the quay, and a fishing boat rested sideways against the steps, but the water no longer climbed the walls.

Mara found Daniel beside the iron ring. He was trying to untie their father’s knot. Each time he loosened one turn, the rope pulled it tight again.

“Leave it,” she said.

Daniel sat back on his heels. “Do you think he knew what was out there?”

Mara looked across the harbor. The five ropes beyond the breakwater had disappeared beneath the surface. Only this one remained visible, stretching from the ring to the skiff, which Mr. Venn had hauled onto the quay.

“I think he knew how to keep it out.”

Mr. Venn came down the steps carrying a canvas bag. He tipped its contents onto a dry stone: a pair of gloves, three rusted shackles, and a notebook swollen with seawater. They had found it under a loose board in the trawler’s wheelhouse.

Mara opened the notebook carefully. Most of the ink had run, but one page had been wrapped in waxed paper. On it, her father had drawn the harbor and its six marks. Beneath the church steps he had written two words: Check annually.

Daniel gave a startled laugh. “He could have told us.”

“He tried,” Mara said, thinking of the chart he had left her.

She shut the notebook. The rope would need replacing before winter, and the outer marks would need finding again. For now, she sat beside Daniel and watched the tide go out."
